scope.scopeNotesMd: This report compares core-package SearchParameter resources and search-related infrastructure metadata for FHIR R4 4.0.1 to FHIR R6 6.0.0-ballot4. The package JSON inventory is treated as authoritative for computable SearchParameter deltas; local rendered HTML pages were used for narrative/provenance context. Findings distinguish direct search behavior and conformance metadata from underlying resource/datatype shape changes. Where a SearchParameter changed only because an element or resource moved, this report records the search runtime impact and delegates the data-model rationale to follow-up dependencies.
outOfScope: Full adjudication of resource removals, renames, splits, or datatype shape changes that caused search expressions to move.
Implementation-guide-specific SearchParameters, profiles, terminology expansions, and server-specific CapabilityStatements outside the two core packages.
OperationDefinition behavior, HTTP status code behavior, and non-search REST behavior except where needed to explain search conformance metadata.
Executing real server searches or validating implementation support beyond the computable core package definitions.

narrativeReportMd:
# SearchParameters R4 to R6 behavior report

## Bottom line
R6 ballot4 contains material SearchParameter behavior and metadata breaks. Many ordinary query codes remain recognizable, but the computable search registry changed substantially: 663 R4 canonical SearchParameter URLs are absent in R6, 536 R6 canonical URLs are new, 184 R4 per-resource canonical/metadata definitions are consolidated into multi-base CanonicalResource/MetadataResource definitions, and 236 exact canonical URL matches have non-metadata field changes.

## Main migration themes
The highest-risk changes are metadata identity churn, type changes on shared search parameters, clinical code/reference splits, Observation value-search narrowing, and one severe canonical repurpose (`medications-date`). Some breaks are direct runtime failures, such as removed Patient extension searches or removed resource endpoints. Others are silent result-set changes, especially expression moves and Observation value searches.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Several R6 goals are reasonable: multi-base metadata definitions reduce duplication, CodeableReference searches need explicit code/reference paths, and `resource`/`special` search types are more precise. However, lower-break alternatives often existed: deprecated aliases for old search codes, preserving old canonical URLs as aliases, accepting old token searches as concept-branch compatibility, or using new canonical URLs instead of repurposing old ones.

## Confidence
Confidence is high for computable inventory counts and field deltas from local package JSON. Confidence is medium for impact prevalence and justification because official rationale, implementation CapabilityStatements, and real server behavior were not available.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 changes the core SearchParameter surface in ways that can break runtime queries, generated clients, and conformance tooling. The most actionable issues are `_content`/`_text`/`_query`/`_profile` type changes, the `ofType` to `of-type` modifier rename, canonical consolidation into CanonicalResource/MetadataResource definitions, `medications-date` being repurposed, CodeableReference search splits, Observation value-search narrowing, and removed Patient extension searches. The main uncertainty is how much compatibility R6 servers will provide beyond the core definitions.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should not match SearchParameters by canonical URL alone. Build a cross-version search registry keyed by resource/base, code, type, expression, and target; then special-case canonical aliases, removed endpoints, split code/reference searches, and expression moves. Update generated client query builders and server indexes together, with regression tests for common clinical searches (`patient`, `subject`, `code`, `date`, `identifier`, `encounter`, `performer`, and `type`).
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Inventory confidence is high because the report loaded all local R4 and R6 core SearchParameter JSON files and package indexes. Impact confidence is medium because the analysis did not execute searches on real servers, did not have official change rationale for every search expression, and did not compare implementation-specific CapabilityStatements. R6 ballot4 content can still change before publication.

inventorySummary.inventoryNotesMd: Counts are from local package JSON, cross-checked against `.index.json` entries. `removedCount` and `addedCount` are canonical URL deltas before inferred replacement matching. `likelyReplacementBySameBaseCodeType` counts removed R4 definitions with at least one R6 added candidate sharing concrete base, code, and type; most of these are CanonicalResource/MetadataResource consolidation rather than query-code removal. Common-URL changes exclude pure status/xpath/processingMode churn but include expression, target, type, base, component, multipleOr, comparator, and name changes.

findings.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile

changedFields.note: The search codes remain stable, but generated search builders, validators, and servers that infer parsing/indexing behavior from type now see different types.
R6 models _profile as a reference to StructureDefinition instead of a URI-valued search.
R6 also makes processingMode explicit on these parameters; this part is metadata-only.

findings.matchRationaleMd: These are exact canonical URL matches for shared resource-level search codes. The material change is not a rename; it is a change in how the same query code is typed and advertised.

impact.impactRationaleMd: `_content`, `_text`, `_query`, and `_profile` are shared infrastructure search parameters. Existing query codes remain recognizable, but clients and conformance tooling that generated string/token/URI parameters from R4 metadata can generate different request syntax or reject R6 metadata. `_profile` is especially visible because URI search and reference search have different modifier/chaining expectations.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: The R4 SearchParameter infrastructure baseline is trial-use/FMM 3, so compatibility matters for common search behavior and conformance metadata, but this is not the normative burden used for Resource or DomainResource structural changes.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A generated R4 client exposes `_profile` as a URI filter and `_text` as a string filter. After loading R6 SearchParameter definitions, the same generator emits a reference-valued `_profile` API and treats `_text`/`_content` as opaque special searches, changing compile-time APIs and possibly accepted modifiers.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: R6 could have kept the R4 SearchParameter.type values for one release while adding narrative that these searches are implemented specially, or could have defined explicit aliases/compatibility text saying URI-form `_profile` and string-form `_text`/`_content` remain accepted.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: Keeping the old type values weakens computable precision for R6 implementations; aliases or compatibility prose reduce generated-code churn without fully preserving a single metadata model.

freshReview.rationaleMd: The search codes did not change, but the type metadata for high-visibility shared parameters did. Because these are common infrastructure parameters and the R4 baseline is moderately mature, the change deserves review to ensure servers still accept the common R4 query forms and document the metadata transition.

evidence.detail: R4 `_content` is type `string`.
R6 `_content` is type `special`.
R4 `_profile` is type `uri` with expression `Resource.meta.profile`.
R6 `_profile` is type `reference` targeting `StructureDefinition`.

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: The strongest runtime mechanism is metadata-driven API/codegen and conformance behavior: an R4 query code may still be sent, but clients and servers infer different parsing, modifiers, and index types from the R6 SearchParameter resource. Servers that treat `special` as a non-string bucket may reject or reinterpret R4-style `_text`, `_content`, or `_query` filters.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Keep acceptance tests for R4-style `_text`, `_content`, `_query`, and `_profile` query strings. When regenerating clients from R6 metadata, verify the generated parameter types and document whether URI-form `_profile` values are still accepted. Server index migrations should treat these as compatibility-sensitive shared parameters, not as ordinary new search codes.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 goal appears to be more accurate computable metadata: full-text and named-query behavior are special, and profiles are canonical references to StructureDefinition. A less-breaking design was partially available: retain the old type values or publish explicit alias/compatibility semantics for one release. The tradeoff is less precise R6 metadata and possible ambiguity in generated APIs.

findings.title: SearchParameter.modifier code `ofType` was replaced by `of-type` while new modifiers were added

changedFields.note: The additive modifiers are not breaking by themselves; the old camelCase `ofType` code is no longer present in the R6 code system.

changedFields.oldValue: missing | exact | contains | not | text | in | not-in | below | above | type | identifier | ofType
changedFields.newValue: missing | exact | contains | not | text | in | not-in | below | above | type | identifier | of-type | code-text | text-advanced | iterate

findings.matchRationaleMd: This finding is based on the SearchParameter resource definition and the bound `search-modifier-code` CodeSystem rather than on one core SearchParameter instance. It affects validation and generation of SearchParameter resources that advertise supported modifiers.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Core R4 SearchParameter instances did not heavily use `modifier`, but custom SearchParameter definitions, CapabilityStatement-derived metadata, validators, and generated query builders can contain or expect `ofType`. R6 removes that exact code and uses `of-type`, so old metadata can fail validation or lose support unless normalized.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: The R4 SearchParameter infrastructure baseline is trial-use/FMM 3, so compatibility matters for common search behavior and conformance metadata, but this is not the normative burden used for Resource or DomainResource structural changes.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A terminology server or profile package carries a custom R4 SearchParameter with `modifier: ["ofType"]`. An R6 validator using the R6 code system rejects that modifier code or a code generator fails to map it to the R6 enum value `of-type`.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: Retain `ofType` as a deprecated alias in the R6 code system while recommending `of-type` in prose and examples.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: The main tradeoff is tolerating two spellings for the same modifier code in metadata, but this is a modest burden compared with breaking existing SearchParameter resources.

freshReview.rationaleMd: This is a small but real wire-code rename in infrastructure metadata. The additive modifiers are fine, but keeping `ofType` as an alias or deprecated code would have avoided a low-value compatibility break.

evidence.detail: R4 includes `ofType` as a search modifier code.
R6 includes `of-type`, `code-text`, `text-advanced`, and `iterate`; it does not include `ofType`.
The R6 SearchParameter.modifier short text lists `of-type` and the new modifier codes.

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: An R4 SearchParameter resource or generated enum value using `ofType` can be old-valid/new-invalid against the R6 modifier code system. Query execution can also be affected where clients or servers derive allowed URL modifiers from this metadata.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Normalize `ofType` to `of-type` when converting SearchParameter metadata to R6. Treat new R6 modifiers as additive. Add regression tests for custom SearchParameter resources and client query builders that previously emitted or consumed `ofType`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The likely R6 goal was to align modifier code spelling with URL modifier spelling and add new search features. That goal could have been met less disruptively by retaining `ofType` as a deprecated alias in the code system for one major release while preferring `of-type` in examples.

findings.title: R6 consolidates many per-resource canonical SearchParameter URLs into multi-base CanonicalResource and MetadataResource definitions

oldSearchParameter.id: ActivityDefinition-date and related per-resource canonical parameters
oldSearchParameter.code: date, status, url, version, context, identifier, related-artifact codes

newSearchParameter.code: same search codes on multi-base definitions

changedFields.note: Computed inventory matched 184 removed R4 per-resource definitions to R6 CanonicalResource-* or MetadataResource-* definitions by base+code+type.

changedFields.oldValue: One primary base resource per SearchParameter
changedFields.newValue: One SearchParameter definition lists many concrete base resources
changedFields.note: The query code is generally preserved where the concrete base remains listed.

changedFields.newValue: Union expression across many base resources
changedFields.note: R6 expressions are broader multi-resource unions.

findings.matchRationaleMd: Canonical URL matching marks the R4 definitions as removed and the R6 definitions as added. Matching by `base[] + code + type` shows they are likely replacements for the same query codes on retained resources; for example, R4 `ActivityDefinition-date` maps to R6 `CanonicalResource-date` because R6 includes `ActivityDefinition` in `base[]` and keeps code `date` and type `date`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Runtime query strings such as `ActivityDefinition?date=` usually remain possible, but canonical SearchParameter identity changes are material for CapabilityStatement.searchParam.definition, generated clients, conformance tests, index registries, and any system that stores support by canonical URL. The blast radius is broad because 184 R4 definitions were matched to CanonicalResource/MetadataResource replacements.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: The R4 SearchParameter infrastructure baseline is trial-use/FMM 3, so compatibility matters for common search behavior and conformance metadata, but this is not the normative burden used for Resource or DomainResource structural changes.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A terminology or quality-measure server advertises `ActivityDefinition-date` and `Library-status` canonical definitions in its R4 CapabilityStatement. An R6 client compares support by canonical URL and concludes those searches are missing because R6 advertises `CanonicalResource-date` and `CanonicalResource-status` instead.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: Keep the old per-resource canonical SearchParameter resources as deprecated aliases that point to the multi-base R6 definitions, or require servers to accept/advertise both old and new definitions during a transition.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: Aliases add registry clutter and require tooling to understand equivalent definitions, but they preserve a stable conformance identity while still allowing R6 to publish normalized multi-base definitions.

freshReview.rationaleMd: The runtime query-code preservation softens the break, but canonical SearchParameter URL is conformance metadata and many generators key on it. A low-cost alias/deprecation strategy appears plausible.

evidence.locator: R4 removed vs R6 added SearchParameter URL diff
evidence.detail: 184 removed R4 definitions had same base+code+type candidates in R6 `CanonicalResource-*` or `MetadataResource-*` definitions.
R4 has a resource-specific canonical `ActivityDefinition-date` with base `ActivityDefinition`, code `date`, type `date`.
R6 has multi-base `CanonicalResource-date` including `ActivityDefinition` with code `date`, type `date`.
R6 similarly consolidates related-artifact searches across metadata resources.

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: The direct mechanism is conformance and metadata tooling rather than a simple query rejection: the same query code on the same endpoint is usually still recognized, but the canonical definition URL changes. Clients that require exact canonical URL matches for supported search parameters may treat an R6 server as not supporting R4 searches.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When comparing capabilities across versions, match search support by resource/base, code, type, and expression in addition to canonical URL. Servers migrating to R6 should consider advertising legacy canonical aliases if their conformance ecosystem depends on exact URLs. Client generators should not assume one SearchParameter definition per resource.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 consolidation is understandable because many metadata resources share canonical fields and related-artifact patterns. A less-breaking base design was available: retain the R4 per-resource canonical definitions as deprecated aliases while introducing the multi-base definitions. That would preserve canonical identity at the cost of duplicate registry entries and equivalence rules.

findings.title: Search parameters whose only R4 bases were removed resources disappear from the R6 search surface

changedFields.oldValue: SearchParameter.base lists R4 resource endpoints such as DocumentManifest, ClinicalImpression, Media, MedicationKnowledge, RequestGroup, and ChargeItem.
changedFields.newValue: Those base resources are not present as R6 core resource endpoints, so their SearchParameters have no same-base R6 definition.
changedFields.note: This report records the search runtime impact but delegates the underlying resource removal/rename rationale to resource/datatype reports.
Computed count of removed R4 SearchParameters whose all base resources are absent from the R6 core resource list.

findings.matchRationaleMd: Canonical URL matching finds these R4 SearchParameters removed. Because their base resources are absent from the R6 core resource inventory, there is no same-base SearchParameter to match. Some have broader model replacements, but those are resource-level migrations rather than direct SearchParameter renames.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 query against a removed endpoint, such as `DocumentManifest?patient=...`, `ClinicalImpression?patient=...`, `Media?subject=...`, or `RequestGroup?patient=...`, has no R6 endpoint or same-base parameter to execute against. The search-layer break is direct, even though the cause is resource model removal or replacement.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: The R4 SearchParameter infrastructure baseline is trial-use/FMM 3, so compatibility matters for common search behavior and conformance metadata, but this is not the normative burden used for Resource or DomainResource structural changes.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A client that indexed documents with `DocumentManifest?patient=` or care orchestration with `RequestGroup?patient=` receives a 404/unsupported resource type or must be rewritten to a different R6 resource and search code.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: Where R6 has a clear replacement resource, a less-breaking search design could define transition aliases or documented redirects for old endpoints and common query codes.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: Endpoint aliases can create long-term support burden and may be impossible when the underlying resource semantics were split, merged, or removed without a one-to-one replacement.

freshReview.rationaleMd: The search break is real, but this report cannot judge proportionality without the resource-level rationale and replacement mappings. The correct action is cross-report review, not duplicating every resource-removal finding here.

evidence.detail: 253 removed R4 SearchParameters had only base resources that are absent from the R6 core resource inventory.
R4 defined patient search on DocumentManifest.
R4 defined patient search on RequestGroup.
R6 core resource inventory does not include DocumentManifest or RequestGroup; RequestOrchestration is a likely replacement to review separately.

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: The old query is rejected at the resource endpoint level before parameter matching: the R4 base resource type is not an R6 core endpoint. Where a replacement exists, the client must know the new endpoint and search parameter mapping.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not migrate these mechanically by SearchParameter URL alone. First resolve the resource migration (for example, RequestGroup to RequestOrchestration where applicable, or DocumentManifest workflows to R6 document/document-reference patterns), then map query codes and result expectations. Add end-to-end tests for each retired endpoint used by applications.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The less-breaking search design depends on the resource-level design. If a one-to-one replacement exists, aliases or redirects for old endpoints and common search codes could reduce disruption. If the resource was split or removed for substantive reasons, preserving the old endpoint may undermine R6 semantics.

findings.title: `medications-date` keeps its canonical URL but moves from MedicationRequest to MedicationAdministration

changedFields.note: The same canonical URL no longer applies to MedicationRequest in R6.

changedFields.oldValue: Returns medication request to be administered on a specific date
changedFields.newValue: Date administration happened (or did not happen)

findings.matchRationaleMd: This is an exact canonical URL match, but the base and expression point to a different resource and meaning. It is not just a resource field rename.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 client using `MedicationRequest?date=` to find requests scheduled for a date cannot use the same R6 SearchParameter. The same canonical definition now describes `MedicationAdministration?date=`, so canonical URL based migration can silently bind a query builder to the wrong endpoint.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: The R4 SearchParameter infrastructure baseline is trial-use/FMM 3, so compatibility matters for common search behavior and conformance metadata, but this is not the normative burden used for Resource or DomainResource structural changes.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A medication reconciliation app generated a `MedicationRequest.date` search from R4 `medications-date`. After loading R6 metadata by canonical URL, the same API method now searches administrations by occurrence, returning a different clinical class of results.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: Define a new canonical URL for the MedicationAdministration date search and either keep `medications-date` on MedicationRequest as deprecated or remove it without reusing the URL for a different base.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: Keeping the old MedicationRequest search may require maintaining an index over timing information that R6 no longer wants as a core query. Using a new URL for the administration query avoids semantic aliasing even if the old search is removed.

freshReview.rationaleMd: Reusing the same canonical URL for a different base and clinical meaning is a high-risk metadata break. Even if R6 wanted to remove MedicationRequest scheduling-date search, the old canonical should not silently point to MedicationAdministration.

evidence.detail: R4 base is MedicationRequest and expression is `MedicationRequest.dosageInstruction.timing.event`.
R6 base is MedicationAdministration and expression is administration occurrence.
This is one of 8 common-URL SearchParameters with base[] changes and is the clearest base repurpose.

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: An old R4 query against MedicationRequest is no longer valid as the same SearchParameter in R6. A metadata-driven client can also accept the same canonical URL but execute against a different resource, producing materially different result sets rather than a clean failure.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Treat `medications-date` as a manual migration item. Preserve separate tests for MedicationRequest authored date (`authoredon` remains) versus scheduled/requested administration timing. Do not map the R4 `medications-date` canonical directly to R6 without checking the base resource.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 goal may have been to align the `date` code with actual administrations rather than requested timing. A less-breaking design was available: publish a new canonical for administration date and leave the R4 MedicationRequest search as deprecated or explicitly removed. Reusing the canonical URL for another base is avoidable.

findings.title: Several common clinical search codes split into code/reference variants or changed type because elements became CodeableReference-like

oldSearchParameter.code: manifestation, reason-given, bodysite, conclusion, event, diagnosis, code

newSearchParameter.code: manifestation-code, manifestation-reference, reason-given-code, conclusioncode-code, conclusioncode-reference, event-code, event-reference, diagnosis-code, diagnosis-reference

changedFields.note: R4 single search codes are removed and R6 publishes explicit code/reference variants.
Some exact canonical URL matches changed from token semantics to reference semantics.

findings.matchRationaleMd: The likely replacements were identified from same base resources, similar descriptions, and expressions that moved from a single CodeableConcept/reference field to explicit `.concept` and `.reference` paths. Exact URL matches with type changes were treated as material field changes rather than renames.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Old token queries can be rejected or return no results when the R6 search code was split or retyped. This affects common clinical workflows such as allergy manifestation, diagnostic report conclusions, document events, encounter diagnosis, medication administration reasons, specimen body site, and service request codes.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: The R4 SearchParameter infrastructure baseline is trial-use/FMM 3, so compatibility matters for common search behavior and conformance metadata, but this is not the normative burden used for Resource or DomainResource structural changes.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: An allergy app issues `AllergyIntolerance?manifestation=http://snomed.info/sct|39579001`. In R6 the old `manifestation` search code is gone; the client must use `manifestation-code` for coded manifestations and a different reference search for observation-backed manifestations.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: Keep old token search codes as deprecated aliases for the `.concept` half where that preserves R4 behavior, and add new `*-reference` searches for the reference half. For exact URL type changes, publish a new reference canonical instead of changing token semantics under the old URL.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: Aliases risk hiding the new reference half and require servers to index both old and new codes, but they avoid breaking common token queries where the old semantics map cleanly to R6 `.concept`.

freshReview.rationaleMd: The R6 modeling goal is coherent: CodeableReference-style data needs separate code and reference search paths. But for common clinical searches, low-cost compatibility aliases for the old token codes would have preserved many R4 queries while steering new clients to precise names.

evidence.detail: R4 has token code `manifestation` over `AllergyIntolerance.reaction.manifestation`.
R6 splits manifestation into token `.concept` and reference `.reference` searches.
R4 `reason-given` is token over `MedicationAdministration.reasonCode`.
R6 same canonical `reason-given` is reference over `MedicationAdministration.reason.reference`; `reason-given-code` is the token replacement.
R6 exact canonical `Specimen-bodysite` is reference targeting BodyStructure rather than token.

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: The old query may be new-invalid because the search code disappeared, or accepted with a different type when an exact canonical changed from token to reference. In the latter case, a token value such as `system|code` can be parsed differently or rejected, while reference values become accepted.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Audit all R4 query builders for renamed clinical code searches. Map old token codes to R6 `*-code` where the old query searched coded concepts, and add separate support for `*-reference` when R6 data can point to resources. Build fixtures where the same clinical fact is represented as a code and as a reference.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 goal of making code/reference search semantics explicit is reasonable. The less-breaking alternative is partial: preserve old token names as aliases for the concept branch while adding new reference searches. That works for many cases but not where the old name is now used for reference semantics under the same canonical URL.

findings.title: Observation value and composite searches no longer include several R4 value forms such as SampledData and CodeableConcept.text

changedFields.oldValue: `Observation.value as Quantity | SampledData` and component/combo equivalents
changedFields.note: R6 quantity searches no longer index SampledData values in the core SearchParameter expressions.
R6 value-string no longer indexes CodeableConcept.text.

changedFields.oldValue: Composite value components referenced R4 value quantity/concept/string definitions that included the broader R4 expressions.
changedFields.newValue: R6 composite components reference the narrowed R6 value expressions.

findings.matchRationaleMd: These are exact canonical URL matches on Observation SearchParameters. The material change is the FHIRPath expression and composite component behavior, not the search code.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Observation search is widely implemented. These changes can silently alter result sets: an R4 query that found waveform/sample observations through SampledData quantity search or coded observations through `value-string` text may be accepted in R6 but no longer match the same records.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: The R4 SearchParameter infrastructure baseline is trial-use/FMM 3, so compatibility matters for common search behavior and conformance metadata, but this is not the normative burden used for Resource or DomainResource structural changes.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A device-observation dashboard searches `Observation?code-value-quantity=...` expecting observations whose numeric series is represented as SampledData. After R6 migration, the query still runs but only Quantity values are indexed, so matching observations disappear without an error.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: Keep legacy Observation value search definitions that include SampledData and CodeableConcept.text as deprecated aliases, or define explicit R6 legacy parameters while documenting preferred precise searches.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: Broader expressions can mix semantically different value forms and may weaken precision. A dedicated legacy alias avoids changing the preferred R6 definition but still requires servers to maintain extra indexes.

freshReview.rationaleMd: The R6 goal may be to make quantity searches only match Quantity and avoid ambiguous SampledData/string semantics. But this is a silent result-set narrowing on a high-use clinical resource; a transitional broader expression or legacy alias deserves review.

evidence.detail: R4 expression includes Quantity and SampledData.
R6 expression includes Quantity only.
R4 expression includes string and CodeableConcept.text.
R6 expression includes string only.
Observation composite code-value and combo-code-value SearchParameters are among the 11 common-URL component changes.

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: The old query is accepted but returns materially different results because the indexed value set is narrower. Composite parameters amplify this because the component value part changes while the composite search code remains stable.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review Observation indexes for SampledData and CodeableConcept.text participation. Add migration tests for `value-quantity`, `combo-value-quantity`, `component-value-quantity`, and `value-string`. If old behavior is required, implement compatibility aliases or custom SearchParameters and document them in CapabilityStatement.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The narrowing may improve type precision, but the same goal could have been met with a less-breaking transitional design: keep the old broad searches as aliases while introducing precise R6 searches. The tradeoff is additional indexes and the risk that old broad semantics continue indefinitely.

findings.title: Reference SearchParameters changed target lists, affecting chaining, type modifiers, and reverse include expectations

oldSearchParameter.id: clinical-patient / clinical-encounter and many resource-specific reference searches
oldSearchParameter.code: patient, subject, encounter, performer, based-on, requester, author

newSearchParameter.id: clinical-patient / clinical-encounter and many resource-specific reference searches
newSearchParameter.code: patient, subject, encounter, performer, based-on, requester, author

changedFields.note: Representative target-list changes; many additional reference parameters add R6 resources and remove deleted R4 resources.

changedFields.oldValue: Large R4 Resource target lists include removed resources such as Media, DocumentManifest, RequestGroup, MolecularSequence, and other retired resources.
changedFields.newValue: R6 target lists replace those with R6 resources such as ImagingSelection, DeviceAlert, RequestOrchestration, SubscriptionTopic, and SubstanceDefinition.

changedFields.oldValue: R4 clients could use target-specific reference modifiers/chains implied by R4 target lists.
changedFields.newValue: R6 target lists can reject old target modifiers or resolve chains through different resources.

findings.matchRationaleMd: Exact canonical URL matches with changed `target[]` were counted across 115 common SearchParameters. This finding groups the runtime effect on reference query behavior rather than listing every target-list edit.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Simple reference equality searches often continue to work, but target lists drive typed reference modifiers, chained search, generated API target enums, and reverse include planning. Old queries such as `patient:Group`, chains through EpisodeOfCare, or references to Media/RequestGroup can be rejected or return different results in R6.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: The R4 SearchParameter infrastructure baseline is trial-use/FMM 3, so compatibility matters for common search behavior and conformance metadata, but this is not the normative burden used for Resource or DomainResource structural changes.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A reporting client issues a typed chain such as `Observation?subject:Group=...` or expects `DiagnosticReport?media=Media/123`. In R6 the target list no longer advertises those targets; the query may be rejected or must be rewritten to new resource targets.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: Where a target resource still exists and the old target is still semantically valid, keep it in the target list for one release. Where the target resource was removed, publish replacement guidance and optionally support local aliases.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: Retaining obsolete targets weakens R6 model clarity and can force support for resources not present in the base package.

freshReview.rationaleMd: The changes mostly follow resource model and reference-target changes. That creates real migration work, but keeping removed or obsolete targets in base R6 target lists could mislead implementations.

evidence.detail: 115 exact canonical URL matches changed `target[]`.
R4 target list is Patient and Group.
R6 target list is Patient.
R4 targets Media.
R6 targets DocumentReference.

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: A reference search with an old type modifier or chain can be rejected as unsupported or can chain through a different target resource. Reverse include behavior can also change because the set of resources considered valid reference targets changed.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory all reference searches using typed modifiers (`:Patient`, `:Group`, etc.) or chaining. Regenerate target enums from R6 metadata and map removed targets to R6 replacements where the underlying resource migration defines one. Test both untyped and typed/chained forms.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: For targets removed with resources, base-compatible preservation is limited. For still-existing targets, R6 could have kept old target entries as deprecated where semantics remained valid. That partial alternative reduces query breaks but may obscure intended R6 target constraints.

findings.title: R4 Patient demographic extension search parameters age, birthOrderBoolean, and mothersMaidenName were removed

changedFields.note: No R6 core SearchParameter with the same Patient base and code was found.

findings.matchRationaleMd: These R4 SearchParameters are canonical-URL removals with no same-base same-code R6 candidates. They are extension-backed Patient searches rather than Patient core element changes.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Patient search is common, and `mothersMaidenName` and age-based matching can be used in identity matching or administrative workflows. R6 removal means an R4 query is rejected unless a server carries custom legacy parameters.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: The R4 SearchParameter infrastructure baseline is trial-use/FMM 3, so compatibility matters for common search behavior and conformance metadata, but this is not the normative burden used for Resource or DomainResource structural changes.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A master-patient-index workflow uses `Patient?mothersMaidenName=Smith` or `Patient?age=67` as part of a demographic match. After moving to a strict R6 core search registry, those query builders no longer have core definitions.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: Retain the R4 extension SearchParameters as deprecated core definitions or publish R6 legacy aliases that point to the same extensions where the extension remains meaningful.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: Age search has dynamic-date semantics and can be expensive or ambiguous; retaining it may encourage non-indexable searches. `mothersMaidenName` can be sensitive and jurisdiction-dependent, but a deprecated alias would not require universal server support.

freshReview.rationaleMd: These are extension-backed searches, but they are on Patient and are low-cost to keep as deprecated extension search aliases. Removal deserves review because identity-matching workflows can be business-critical.

evidence.detail: R4 defines Patient code `age` with number type and dynamic-age description.
R4 defines Patient code `mothersMaidenName` over a Patient extension.
R6 Patient search codes omit age, birthOrderBoolean, and mothersMaidenName.

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: The old R4 query code is no longer recognized as a core Patient SearchParameter. A strict R6 server rejects the query or treats it as a custom unsupported parameter; generated clients lose the corresponding methods.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Check whether applications use these Patient extension searches. If so, define local R6 SearchParameters or profile-specific search capabilities and advertise them explicitly. Avoid assuming core R6 support. For age search, test date-boundary and deceased-patient semantics if implemented locally.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A less-breaking design was available for at least `mothersMaidenName` and `birthOrderBoolean`: keep the extension-backed SearchParameters as deprecated aliases. The age search is more debatable because it has dynamic semantics, but it could have been retained with clearer implementation guidance.

findings.title: Bundle composition and message searches changed from reference search to the new resource search type
findings.matchRationaleMd: These are exact canonical URL matches on Bundle search parameters. R6 keeps the same search codes but changes type and expression to the new `resource` type.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Document/message Bundle discovery is important for exchange workflows. R4 metadata described these as reference searches to Composition or MessageHeader; R6 describes them as resource searches over the first embedded resource. Query builders and conformance tests that expect reference syntax or targets will need changes.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: The R4 SearchParameter infrastructure baseline is trial-use/FMM 3, so compatibility matters for common search behavior and conformance metadata, but this is not the normative burden used for Resource or DomainResource structural changes.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A document repository client generated `Bundle?composition=Composition/123` from R4 reference metadata. In R6, the parameter is advertised as type `resource`, so the generated method and server parser are different even though the search concept is still first-entry Composition.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: R6 could have kept deprecated reference-style aliases for `composition` and `message` while introducing new resource-typed definitions or clearer syntax guidance.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: Keeping the old reference type would preserve generated APIs but would continue to misrepresent the indexed element and could block use of the new resource search type.

freshReview.rationaleMd: This is a real metadata/API break on a mature exchange resource, but the R6 type is semantically more accurate because `Bundle.entry[0].resource` is an embedded resource, not a Reference element.

evidence.detail: R4 type is reference, expression `Bundle.entry[0].resource`, target Composition.
R6 type is resource, expression `Bundle.entry[0].resource as Composition`, no target list.
R4 search-param-type did not include `resource`.
R6 search-param-type adds `resource`.

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: Generated clients and servers switch from reference-search parsing/indexing to resource-search parsing/indexing for the same Bundle query codes. Old reference-style values may be rejected or handled by compatibility logic outside the core definition.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Regenerate Bundle query builders and verify actual accepted query syntax for `composition` and `message`. If R4 reference-style values are used in production, add compatibility tests or server aliases. Update CapabilityStatement searchParam definitions and documentation to reflect type `resource`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 goal is likely to correct the type model for searching embedded resources. A less-breaking transition could preserve old reference-style aliases. The tradeoff is duplicate metadata and the risk that clients continue to treat embedded-resource searches as ordinary Reference searches.

findings.title: StructureDefinition ext-context changed from a token search to a composite search with new component parameters
findings.matchRationaleMd: This is an exact canonical URL match whose type, expression, multipleOr, and components changed. The new R6 token components make the old single token search only one part of the new composite semantics.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Extension registries and IG tooling commonly search StructureDefinition extension context. An R4 `ext-context` token query over context type is not equivalent to the R6 composite parameter and may be rejected or need component syntax.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: The R4 SearchParameter infrastructure baseline is trial-use/FMM 3, so compatibility matters for common search behavior and conformance metadata, but this is not the normative burden used for Resource or DomainResource structural changes.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: An IG publishing tool searches `StructureDefinition?ext-context=element` to find extensions valid at element context. In R6 the same search code is composite and the token-only query must be rewritten to `ext-context-type` or a composite form.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: Keep `ext-context` token semantics as deprecated and add a new composite code, or make the old token query equivalent to the `ext-context-type` component during a transition.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: Aliases require extra server logic and may leave two ways to search extension context, but they avoid breaking common IG tooling.

freshReview.rationaleMd: The R6 composite design can represent context type plus expression more precisely, but reusing the old code for a composite changes runtime syntax. Keeping the old token search as an alias appears low-cost.

evidence.detail: R4 `ext-context` is token over `StructureDefinition.context.type`.
R6 `ext-context` is composite over `StructureDefinition.context` with type and expression components.
R6 adds separate token component SearchParameters.

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: The old token-valued query can be rejected because the same search code now expects composite behavior. Even if accepted, it no longer fully expresses the R6 context search semantics.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Update extension-registry and IG tooling to use `ext-context-type` for the old token use case or the full composite `ext-context` form where both type and expression are needed. Add compatibility tests for extension lookup by context type.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 goal of more precise extension context search is reasonable. A less-breaking design was available: preserve `ext-context` as the context-type token search and introduce a new composite code for type+expression. That would avoid changing syntax for existing extension lookup workflows.

findings.title: Many stable search codes now index different R6 element paths after resource model changes

changedFields.note: These examples represent stable search codes whose underlying R6 element path moved.
Computed count of exact canonical URL matches with expression changes.

findings.matchRationaleMd: Exact canonical URL and search code matching shows these are not renames. The R6 expression changed, often because the underlying data-model path moved or the search now repeats through a different backbone.

impact.impactRationaleMd: For migrated data that is correctly transformed to R6, many queries preserve intent. The risk is silent result-set change when historical data, partial migrations, custom stores, or compatibility servers still populate R4-shaped paths or when the R6 expression intentionally narrows/broadens the old semantics.

fmmContext.rationaleMd: The R4 SearchParameter infrastructure baseline is trial-use/FMM 3, so compatibility matters for common search behavior and conformance metadata, but this is not the normative burden used for Resource or DomainResource structural changes.

freshReview.realWorldScenarioMd: A document index migrates DocumentReference but forgets to map `context.period` to the R6 period field. `DocumentReference?period=` still runs in R6, but the server index uses a different path and returns fewer records until data and indexing are migrated together.

lessBreakingAlternative.candidateDesignMd: For common paths, define transitional expressions that index both old and new paths in compatibility servers, or keep old search aliases where the old path still has a clear meaning.
lessBreakingAlternative.tradeoffsOrReasonMd: Base R6 cannot generally index removed R4 paths that no longer exist in valid R6 instances. Broad transitional expressions can also hide incomplete data migration.

freshReview.rationaleMd: Most expression moves follow underlying model changes and are proportionate when data migration is handled. The compatibility concern is silent result-set drift, not necessarily bad R6 design.

evidence.detail: 125 exact canonical URL matches changed `expression`.
R4 searches `Organization.address`.
R6 searches `Organization.contact.address`.
R4 searches `DocumentReference.context.period`.
R6 searches `DocumentReference.period`.

findings.runtimeMechanismMd: The query code is accepted, but the server evaluates a different FHIRPath expression and indexes different elements. If data migration and index migration are not aligned, the same query returns materially different result sets.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For every stable search code used in production, compare the R4 and R6 expressions and update indexes after data transformation. Prioritize high-volume resources and query codes. Add before/after fixtures where the same logical fact moved paths in R6.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because many expression changes are downstream of data-model moves, a fully less-breaking base search design is not always available. However, for common paths, R6 could document compatibility aliases or broader transitional expressions. That is a partial alternative with index complexity and semantic-precision tradeoffs.

checkedNoMaterialChange.area: Search framework transport and result controls
checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Reviewed local R4/R6 search framework pages for transport and common result-control concepts such as `_count`, `_total`, `_sort`, `_summary`, `_elements`, `_include`, `_revinclude`, and `_filter`. No core package SearchParameter inventory delta indicated a direct breaking change to those generic controls; this report focuses on computable SearchParameter definition changes.

`_id`, `_lastUpdated`, `_tag`, `_security`, and `_source` keep the same canonical URLs, codes, base scopes, types, and expressions. R6 status/processingMode metadata changed, but no material query semantics change was found for these parameters.

checkedNoMaterialChange.area: Comparator support on ordinary date/quantity/number parameters
checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: Comparator arrays were stable for ordinary date/quantity/number SearchParameters inspected in the exact-URL diff. The only computed comparator delta was on an example SearchParameter, not a core production search behavior finding.
No broad change in multipleAnd/multipleOr behavior was found. One material multipleOr change is included in the StructureDefinition `ext-context` composite finding.

The report found material changes to SearchParameter canonical definitions that can affect CapabilityStatement.searchParam.definition values, but did not find a separate generic CapabilityStatement structural search-advertisement break. Implementation-specific CapabilityStatements were not compared.

No separate compartment-framework break was found beyond changed patient/encounter SearchParameter bases and reference targets captured in findings. Actual compartment membership behavior should be validated against compartment definitions and server implementations.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds explicit SearchParameter.processingMode values, usually `normal`
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: For exact URL matches, `processingMode: normal` generally makes implicit R4 behavior explicit. It is metadata churn unless tooling treats absence versus `normal` as a semantic difference.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Regenerate SearchParameter models to include `processingMode`; do not treat missing R4 value as a custom mode.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Most retained core SearchParameters changed status from draft to active
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Status maturation changes conformance metadata but does not by itself change query syntax or result matching.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Dashboards may see many metadata status changes; filter them separately from runtime search changes.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds many searches for new resources and new R6 element paths
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: New optional SearchParameters on new or expanded R6 resources are additive unless they replace an R4 query code or canonical identity, which is covered in findings.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Client generators should add these as R6-only capabilities and avoid assuming R4 support.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: New R6 modifier codes `code-text`, `text-advanced`, and `iterate` are additive
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The new modifier codes expand R6 capability. The breaking portion is the `ofType` to `of-type` rename, which is reported separately.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code generators should add enum values for the new modifiers while preserving a migration mapping for `ofType`.

followUpDependencies.nameOrUrl: Removed or replaced R4 resources with SearchParameter bases
followUpDependencies.reasonMd: SearchParameters on removed resources produce direct old-query failures, but the rationale and migration mapping depend on resource-level reports for DocumentManifest, ClinicalImpression, Media, MedicationKnowledge, RequestGroup, ChargeItem, and other removed bases.

followUpDependencies.nameOrUrl: CodeableReference and element splits in clinical resources
followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Many search code splits and token/reference type changes are search impacts of underlying CodeableReference-style data-model changes. Resource reports should confirm the intended migration for each affected path.

Observation search narrowing depends on R6 value datatype semantics and should be checked with the Observation data-model report and implementation expectations for SampledData and CodeableConcept.text.

Canonical SearchParameter consolidation materially affects conformance metadata. Implementation CapabilityStatements should be compared to see whether servers advertise old aliases, new multi-base definitions, or both.
The `ofType` to `of-type` code change should be reviewed with terminology/code-system migration policy to decide whether an alias should be retained.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The analysis used local package JSON and rendered pages but did not have an official, curated R4-to-R6 SearchParameter change log explaining intent for each change.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: An official HL7 SearchParameter diff with rationale and replacement mappings would improve justification and less-breaking-alternative confidence.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: R6 input is ballot4/build content, not a final normative release. SearchParameter definitions, resource inventory, and narrative guidance may change before publication.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Repeat the inventory comparison against the final R6 core package.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No R4 or R6 server was queried. Runtime behavior was inferred from core SearchParameter definitions, so server compatibility aliases or stricter rejections are unknown.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run representative R4 and R6 queries against reference and production servers and compare CapabilityStatements.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Many search expression and target changes are downstream of resource/datatype model changes. This report identifies the search impact but does not fully adjudicate the underlying model design.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review corresponding resource/datatype reports and merge findings using dependency IDs rather than duplicating StructureDefinition findings.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Local rendered pages were reviewed for relevant search framework and resource-definition context, but this was not a formal semantic diff of every narrative paragraph.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: A section-by-section narrative diff of search.html, searchparameter.html, capabilitystatement.html, and compartmentdefinition.html would improve confidence in framework-level no-change conclusions.
